title: AI in banking: what are community banks actually using it for?
description: AI in banking for community banks and credit unions: where it pays first, from fraud to CECL and loan review. Which guidance applies, and who signs off.
verdict: Generative AI is spreading fast at banks and credit unions, but few run AI across the whole institution.[^1][^2]
Fraud detection leads AI use at community banks; credit unions also use AI to help contact-center staff.[^2][^3]
Your core provider is the gate: three in four banks need it to reach their own data.[^4][^5]
For CECL, put AI on the paperwork, not the math: documentation and Q-factor support are where exams and costs bite.[^66][^67]
Fair lending still applies: you owe specific denial reasons, and some states kept disparate impact.[^8][^9]

headings.ranked: Where does AI pay first at a community bank or credit union?
headings.rules: Which rules apply to AI at a community bank or credit union?
headings.what-goes-wrong: Where does AI go wrong at community banks and credit unions?
headings.buy-or-build: Should you buy AI from your core and vendors, or build it?

summary: AI at a community bank or credit union mostly sorts, drafts and answers: fraud alerts, credit memos, staff questions.[^2][^3] What changes is time: large bank TD cut first-draft credit memos from up to 3 days to under 30 minutes.[^10] People still decide, and core data access makes or breaks it.[^11][^4]
humanRole: Your people keep every credit decision, every BSA filing and the member conversation, and management owns oversight of every AI vendor.[^11][^12]

Credit officers keep each credit decision and sign every memo AI drafts; TD sends its AI drafts to expert review.[^10] The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) rates AI risk partly by whether a person approves each output.[^12][^13]
Your CFO and chief credit officer set each Q-factor (qualitative adjustment to the loss estimate) and sign its reason.[^66] Management must document the allowance method before use.[^73]

Your Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) officer decides what gets filed; AI only sorts alerts first, as Fiserv's triage agent does (vendor).[^14] Most alerts are false positives, so that sorting is where analyst time goes.[^15]
Member-service staff keep the conversation; AI suggests answers from your own procedures.[^3] In a 5,172-agent study, AI help raised issues resolved per hour about 15%, most for newer staff.[^16]

Management owns vendor oversight: using a vendor does not reduce your responsibility.[^11][^17] Census data shows 66% of firms where AI changed tasks use it only to help staff; 2% report employment decreases.[^18]

ranked.name: Fraud and anti-money-laundering (AML) alert triage
ranked.why: Of community banks using AI, 77% use it for fraud detection and security.[^2] About 90-95% of anti-money-laundering alerts are false positives, so analysts spend most of their time clearing noise.[^15]
ranked.payoff: Analyst minutes per alert, and the share of alerts closed as false positives.

ranked.name: Commercial credit spreading and memo drafts
ranked.why: At TD, an AI tool cut first-draft credit memos from up to 3 days to under 30 minutes.[^10] Experts passed 95% of drafts on 220 deals; TD is a large bank, so treat that as a ceiling.[^10]
ranked.payoff: Hours from complete financials to a signed credit memo.

ranked.name: Staff knowledge search and contact-center agent assist
ranked.why: Among credit unions using AI in the contact center, 80% run generative AI agent assist.[^3] In a large published study, AI help raised issues resolved per hour about 15%.[^16]
ranked.payoff: Handle time and first-contact resolution, checked against a weekly sample of answers.

ranked.name: Loan files and back-office documents
ranked.why: APQC's median cost to process one invoice is $6.00, a fair yardstick for any paper-heavy step.[^19] Machine reading costs $1.50 per 1,000 pages on AWS Textract's price list.[^20]
ranked.payoff: Minutes per loan file or exception cleared, and re-keying errors caught.

ranked.name: CECL (current expected credit loss) paperwork: Q-factor support, documentation and validation prep
ranked.why: Fed exams of nearly 200 banks found the weak spots were documentation and Q-factor support, not the math.[^66] One American Bankers Association (ABA) example: a 28-page Q-factor update and a 125-question audit checklist.[^67]
ranked.payoff: Hours per quarter on the Q-factor packet and on audit or validation prep.

ranked.name: Loan portfolio monitoring and loan review scope
ranked.why: Examiners ask for covenant, stale-statement and annual review tracking reports, which portfolio analytics can produce.[^84] The 2020 interagency guidance lets risk indicators set loan review scope and frequency.[^83]
ranked.payoff: Days to answer the exam request list, and stale items caught before the examiner finds them.

ranked.name: Consumer credit decisioning
ranked.why: Two in three credit unions plan AI credit decisioning, per America's Credit Unions.[^21] It takes the most work: fair lending tests and specific reasons for every denial.[^8][^22]
ranked.payoff: Share of applications auto-decided, with approval and delinquency rates by group.

ranked.name: Member chatbots and voice AI
ranked.why: One credit union told Congress its voice AI handles over 60% of business-hours calls.[^23] The CFPB found chatbots giving wrong answers and trapping people in loops.[^24]
ranked.payoff: Share of calls and chats resolved without a hand-off, and complaints about the bot.

ranked.name: Share of wallet and next products for existing customers
ranked.why: In a McKinsey study, relationship managers with analytics tools grew portfolios 9%, against 5% for a control group.[^25] Many banks have not yet linked accounts into households, which comes first.[^26]
ranked.payoff: Products per household, and new accounts opened by existing customers.

ownData.title: Who examines you, and which AI guidance applies?
ownData.intro: Your charter decides: the OCC, Fed or FDIC examines banks and NCUA credit unions, each pointing to its own AI-related guidance.[^31][^6][^7][^30] On 26 Nov 2026 we counted banks holding $250M to $5B by federal regulator in FDIC data, assets as of 30 Sep 2026.[^28] Credit union counts come from NCUA data for Q2 2026.[^29]
headers: AI guidance your examiner points to
rows: National bank or federal savings association (OCC)
OCC 2026-13 model guidance, aimed at banks over $30B.[^31] OCC's AI exam framework, which sets no new expectations.[^12]
State member bank (Federal Reserve, with your state)
SR 26-2, with the same $30B focus.[^6] The Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) AI framework, if your state adopts it.[^32]
State nonmember bank (FDIC, with your state)
FIL-15-2026, which 'generally does not apply' at $30B or less.[^7] The CSBS framework, if your state adopts it.[^32]
Generative and agentic AI sit outside the April 2026 model guidance.[^6][^7]
Not counted for this exact band
No AI-specific rules; NCUA points to letters 07-CU-13 and 01-CU-20.[^30] NCUA cannot examine your vendors directly.[^33]
Federally insured state credit union (NCUA, with your state)
Not counted for this exact band
The same NCUA letters.[^30] Ask your state regulator about its own approach.
About 748 hold over $500M (third-party reads of NCUA data)[^34][^35]
NCUA joined the Sep 2026 proposed vendor guidance.[^36]

tables.intro: Fiserv sells agentOS agents for loan onboarding and AML triage, Jack Henry builds on Google Cloud, and FIS works with Anthropic.[^14][^44][^46] These big three cores serve over 70% of banks and nearly half of credit unions.[^43] The American Bankers Association (ABA) says some cores charge extra for data connections (APIs), and extraction can take 12 to 18 months.[^5]

tables.title: Where does AI fit in the quarterly CECL close, and who signs?
tables.intro: Your method still runs as usual: the Fed's SCALE spreadsheet, NCUA's WARM (weighted-average remaining maturity) tool or a vendor model.[^27][^77] Most community banks use a vendor: 70% in an ABA count.[^68] We found no independent figure for AI time saved on CECL work.

rows.name: Data check
cells: Reconciles the loan trial balance to the general ledger and Call Report segments, and flags breaks and missing risk ratings.
The accounting lead clears each break and documents segment choices, a weak spot in Fed exams.[^66]

rows.name: Run the method
cells: Nothing new: SCALE, WARM or the vendor model runs as before.[^27][^77]
The CFO confirms the inputs and the forecast choice.

rows.name: Q-factor packet
cells: Gathers local unemployment, commercial real estate vacancy, concentration and policy-exception trends, then drafts the narrative with each figure cited.[^67]
The CFO and chief credit officer set each Q-factor and sign the reason. Peer data is context only; targeting a peer median is inappropriate.[^73]

rows.name: Back-test
cells: Compares last year's estimate with actual losses and drafts the variance note.
The reviewer accepts or revises it. A Q-factor may adjust for that variance.[^73]

rows.name: Validation and audit prep
cells: Builds the document index against the validator's or auditor's checklist.[^67]
An independent validator or auditor concludes. Auditors may still expect full validation.[^69]

rows.name: Approval
cells: Nothing.
Management proposes the allowance; the audit committee and the board approve it.

tables.note: Illustrative steps, built from Fed exam findings and ABA cost reports.[^66][^67] Start with one quarter's Q-factor packet before changing anything else. Not accounting advice.

rules.name: Model risk guidance: SR 26-2, OCC 2026-13, FDIC FIL-15-2026
rules.what: Replaces SR 11-7 and is 'most relevant' above $30B in assets.[^6][^31] The FDIC says it generally doesn't apply at $30B or less without significant model risk.[^7] Generative and agentic AI are outside its scope.[^47][^48]

rules.name: OCC Bulletin 2026-54: framework for Super Intelligence
rules.what: How OCC examiners will look at AI, which the bulletin calls Super Intelligence. It sets no new expectations and can be tailored to community banks.[^12][^49] Its vendor items include change notice, liability and vendor training on your data.[^50]

rules.name: CSBS AI Supervisory Framework
rules.what: An optional tool for state examiners, built on the AI Risk Management Framework from NIST, the federal standards body.[^32][^51] It covers AI inside vendor products and doesn't apply to national banks.[^51][^52]

rules.name: Interagency third-party guidance (2023) and proposed revision (2026)
rules.status: 2023 guidance in force for banks; revision proposed 11 Sep 2026
rules.what: Using a vendor doesn't reduce your responsibility.[^11][^17] The proposal says the 2023 guidance was read too broadly and would replace it; NCUA joined.[^40][^36]

rules.name: Joint statement on community banks and core service providers
rules.what: Examiners may weigh opaque pricing, back billing, excessive deconversion fees and limits on third-party integration.[^41] Bring it to your next core contract talk.

rules.name: NCUA Super Intelligence (SI) page
rules.what: NCUA says it has no AI-specific rules and points to letters 07-CU-13 and 01-CU-20 on vendor due diligence.[^30] NCUA can't examine vendors directly, so that checking falls on you.[^33]

rules.name: Regulation B (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) final rule
rules.status: In force since 21 Jul 2026; litigation pending
rules.what: Removes the federal disparate impact (effects) test and narrows 'discouragement'.[^53][^22] Adverse action notices under 12 CFR 1002.9 still need specific reasons, even from complex models.[^8][^54] A suit challenging the rule is pending.[^55]

rules.name: State fair lending law
rules.status: Varies by state; New Jersey rule adopted Dec 2025
rules.what: New Jersey kept disparate impact in its lending rule.[^9] Massachusetts settled for $2.5M with a student lender over an AI model it had not tested for disparate impact.[^56]

rules.name: Interagency policy statement on allowances for credit losses
rules.what: Applies to banks and NCUA-insured credit unions alike.[^73] Management must evaluate and document models before use, and setting the allowance to a peer median is inappropriate.[^73]

rules.name: OCC Bulletin 2025-26: model risk management for community banks
rules.what: Community banks are not required to validate models every year.[^72] Examiners give no negative feedback solely for validation frequency or scope.[^72] Auditors may still ask for full validation.[^69]

rules.name: FASB (Financial Accounting Standards Board) review of CECL
rules.status: Final report expected by end of 2026
rules.what: The review has not changed CECL so far.[^74][^75] Fed Vice Chair Bowman urged repeal or a community bank exemption, in a letter giving her own view.[^70] Experts expect little change.[^71]

rules.name: Interagency Guidance on Credit Risk Review Systems (SR 20-13)
rules.status: In force since May 2020; NCUA joined
rules.what: The board approves a written loan review policy, typically yearly, and reviewers stay independent of approval.[^83] Small or rural institutions may use modified independence.[^83]

watchOuts: It goes wrong through member data pasted into personal AI, wrong chatbot answers, vendor models without denial reasons and core contracts that block your data.[^39][^24][^8][^5] Each fix is below.
Staff paste member data into personal ChatGPT or Gemini accounts, as ICBA warns.[^39] Approve one business tool and write down that member data stays out of anything else, as CU*Answers does.[^57]
Chatbots give wrong answers or trap members in loops, which the CFPB flagged.[^24] Keep a fast path to a person, and test fees and rates, which the OCC names as hallucination risks.[^12]
A vendor's credit model can't give the specific reasons a denial needs.[^8][^58] Before you sign, have the vendor show the reasons its model gives on a sample of your own denials.
Treating the April 2026 Reg B rule as the end of fair lending risk.[^22] State law can still reach disparate impact, so keep testing outcomes by group.[^9][^56]
Core contracts that block integration or charge for your own data.[^5][^41] Read the contract before you pick an AI vendor, and cite the 2026 joint statement at renewal.

Deepfake video and voice used to open accounts or fool call centers, per Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.[^59] Add a callback or second check before changing account details or moving money.
Buying a complex machine-learning loss model before FASB's review lands.[^74] Its final report is due by the end of 2026 and experts expect little change, so keep your current method for now.[^71]
Setting Q-factors to land on a peer median, which the 2023 policy statement calls inappropriate.[^73] Use peer data as context only, and write down why each factor moved.[^66]

faq.q: Where should a community bank or credit union start with AI?
faq.a: Most start with drafting tools and the fraud tools their vendors already sell.[^4][^2] Pilot one workflow on one team or branch, with a before-and-after number such as analyst minutes per alert.

faq.q: Can AI make credit decisions at a community bank or credit union?
faq.a: Yes, but you owe specific reasons for every denial and must keep application records for 25 months, 12 for business credit.[^8][^54] The OCC also rescinded its 1997 credit scoring exam guidance in April 2026.[^31]

faq.q: What does NCUA expect from credit unions using AI?
faq.a: NCUA has no AI-specific rules; its existing rules and vendor due diligence letters apply.[^30] It can't examine your vendors directly, so that work falls on you.[^33]

faq.q: Did the April 2026 Reg B rule end fair lending risk for AI models?
faq.a: No. Federal disparate impact is gone, but intentional discrimination, the Fair Housing Act and state law still apply.[^22][^55][^9] Adverse action notices are unchanged.[^54]

faq.q: What does AI cost a community bank or credit union?
faq.a: Drafting tools run about $20 to $21 per user a month, prices read 26 Nov 2026.[^60][^61] Alkami lists data and marketing tiers from $23K a year (vendor).[^62] Core providers' AI, such as Fiserv's credit pricing, isn't published, so get a scoped quote.[^14]

faq.q: Will examiners criticize us for using AI?
faq.a: Not for using AI by itself: the OCC says its AI framework sets no new expectations and can be tailored to community banks.[^12][^49] The FDIC says not following its model guidance does not, by itself, bring criticism.[^7]

faq.q: Who is required to comply with CECL?
faq.a: Every bank and federally insured credit union follows CECL under the 2023 interagency policy statement, except credit unions under $10M, which are exempt by statute.[^73][^76] Small banks need no sophisticated model, per the OCC.[^80]

faq.q: Can machine learning improve our CECL estimate?
faq.a: Not at most community banks yet: we found no independent evidence that machine learning beats SCALE or WARM at small banks.[^80] Across a full cycle, logistic regression held up better in a Boston Fed study, and small portfolios are often too thin for statistics.[^78][^79] Use AI on the documentation and Q-factor evidence instead.[^66][^67]

faq.q: What does CECL cost a community bank?
faq.a: One bank spent $475K to implement CECL and $260K+ a year to run it, a figure Fed Vice Chair Bowman cited in her own op-ed.[^71][^70] Of community banks, 70% pay vendors for CECL, per the ABA; the Risk Management Association (RMA) found 4 in 5 in 2022.[^68][^81] RMA's 2021 survey put full validation of one vendor model at $75K or more.[^82]

faq.q: Do we need an annual CECL model validation?
faq.a: No, not if the OCC supervises you: its Bulletin 2025-26 says community banks need not validate models every year.[^72] A SCALE or WARM spreadsheet may fall outside the 2026 guidance's definition of a model, which excludes simple spreadsheet arithmetic.[^6][^7] Your auditor may still expect full validation, per the ABA.[^69]

Not as of 26 Nov 2026: FASB's review has not changed CECL, and its final report is due by year-end.[^74][^75] Fed Vice Chair Bowman urged repeal or a community bank exemption, in a letter giving her own view.[^70] Experts expect little change.[^71]

faq.q: How should a community bank analyze its loan portfolio?
faq.a: Track concentrations, risk-rating migration, past-dues, stale financials and covenant exceptions, then let those trends pick your loan review sample.[^84][^83] Examiners ask for financial statement, covenant and annual review tracking reports.[^84] AI can build those reports; the chief credit officer approves the review scope.[^83][^85]

buyVsBuild.buy: Mostly buy, when your core or an established vendor already sells the job, such as fraud triage or memo drafting.[^14][^44] ICBA told the OCC that partnering with a core provider is often the only practical path for community banks.[^46] Most enterprise AI is now bought: 76% of use cases, up from 53% in 2024.[^63]
buyVsBuild.build: Build only thin layers where your own procedures are the edge, such as a staff knowledge base. MIT research found bought tools succeed about 67% of the time; internal builds about a third as often.[^64][^63] For credit models, buy and validate; you still owe specific denial reasons.[^8]

pickElse: When your core already sells the AI job: check Fiserv agentOS, Jack Henry's Google Cloud tools or FIS before adding a separate vendor.[^14][^44][^46]
Staff only need drafting and summaries: Microsoft 365 Copilot ($21 per user a month) or ChatGPT Business ($20), prices read 26 Nov 2026.[^60][^61] Copilot is what 95% of AI-using banks report.[^4]
You need a CECL estimate: the Fed's free SCALE tool serves banks under $1B, and NCUA's free WARM-based tool serves credit unions under $100M.[^27][^77]
Consumer credit decisions: buy from a specialist such as Zest AI, which claims 25% higher approvals, then validate it yourself.[^65][^8]

offer.heading: Which two AI jobs can your core already support?
offer.body: Usually fraud and AML alert triage first, then commercial loan onboarding, credit memo drafts or CECL paperwork. In a free 30-minute call we check what your own core and vendors sell, and which guidance applies to your charter.

reviews.notes: Dana (COO): the new CECL and loan review items read well, but ABA and RMA appeared before they were spelled out, because the ranked list sits above the core table. Both are now spelled out where they first appear.

Ops head: in the CECL close table, the 'who decides' column for the data check held an exam finding instead of a task. It now says the accounting lead clears breaks and documents segment choices, the weak spot Fed exams found.

GM: CECL is institution-wide, so asked what a small first step looks like. The CECL table note now says to start with one quarter's Q-factor packet. Loan monitoring keeps a measurable payoff: days to answer the exam request list.

Head of lending: wanted CECL in the bottom line and no claim that machine learning beats SCALE or WARM. The model risk bullet (still covered in the charter table and rules) gave way to a CECL bullet on paperwork, not math. The FAQ says plainly we found no evidence ML wins at small banks; Bowman's repeal call is labelled her own view; the RMA $75K is labelled 2021; no CSBS 11% figure is used.

Steve: the CECL cost answer gives a number first, from a named source, with the vendor share next to it. The offer now lists CECL among the work mapped in the free call. No Zavient price, per site rules.

answers.human-role: People keep every decision: credit officers sign each memo, your BSA officer decides what gets filed, and staff keep the member conversation.[^10][^14][^3] Management still owns vendor oversight.[^11][^17]
answers.ranked: Fraud and anti-money-laundering alert triage pays first, then commercial credit memo drafts and staff knowledge search.[^2][^15][^10][^3]
answers.rules: Fair lending law and vendor oversight duties apply to every charter. The April 2026 model risk guidance mostly targets banks over $30B.[^8][^11][^30][^6] OCC-supervised banks also face the OCC's AI framework.[^12] For CECL, the 2023 interagency allowance policy statement applies to every charter.[^73]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI goes wrong when staff paste member data into personal accounts, chatbots give wrong answers, or a vendor's credit model can't give the specific reasons a denial needs.[^39][^24][^8]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your core already sells the job, staff only need drafting, a bank under $1B needs a CECL estimate, or credit decisions need a specialist vendor.[^14][^60][^27][^65]
answers.table-4: AI fits the paperwork around your allowance method: data checks, the Q-factor packet, variance notes and the audit index.[^66][^67] People sign: the CFO and chief credit officer set each Q-factor, and the audit committee and board approve the allowance.[^73]
